topic: Losing four-part positions in normal-play CRIM; Bašić–Gottlieb–Krnc (2026), Section 5, Question 1, p. 17
title: Bašić–Gottlieb–Krnc (2026), Section 5, Question 1 (p. 17): an alternative four-part proof after Mehat (2026), with explicit strategies and small-row stacking

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: For Bašić–Gottlieb–Krnc (2026), Section 5, Question 1, p. 17, we give an alternative proof of Mehat's classification (23 August 2026) of all losing four-part positions in normal-play CRIM, with no bound on the part sizes. For a >= b >= c >= d >= 1, the largest part a must be even; four disjoint cases involving d, c and the parity of b give the remaining conditions. The proof identifies every possible column move by its height and gives an explicit winning move in each complementary case. Consequences include even-rank necessity and hook-stacking closure with at most four rows or columns, the odd-gap winning-move conclusion through six rows or columns using Mehat's rank theorem, exact padding formulas for one- and two-part inputs, and an explanation of 21 of the 38 diagrams in their Appendix A.
summary: Alternative proof of Mehat's four-part classification, explicit winning moves, small-row hook stacking, six-row odd-gap consequences, padding formulas, and checked boundary counterexamples with prior attribution.

coverage.four_part_outcome: Theorem 1; all positive a >= b >= c >= d, without a size bound
coverage.three_part_boundary: The all-one column [1,1,1] is winning; the corrected full three-part classification has a written proof
coverage.consequences: Written proofs for even-rank necessity and losing-hook stacking with at most four rows or columns; first-row/first-column moves through six rows or columns using Mehat Corollary 3; exact padding and appending formulas on one- and two-part inputs
coverage.finite_checks: All 46,376 partitions with at most four parts and largest part at most 30; 40,920 four-part positions, 15,761 losing; thirteen strategy branches; Mehat parity-table comparison; 7,149 hook stacks and their conjugates; all 38 Appendix A diagrams

coverage.boundary_declaration: D5.S0.Certificates.Games.CrimRectairSquareBoundaryRefutation.result negates the printed universal square-rectair formula using r=1, k=0; no replacement for r>=2 is asserted
